Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

by preposition

the means: how something is done

also by means of, through, by doing, on foot, by hand, by letter

classical

Cic. Att. 5.9.1: iter facere pedibus
Cic. Off. 1.105: mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

cāsus ablātīvus

construction: the means in the ablative, with no preposition

by, through (the means)

The ordinary way: pedibus, on foot; manū, by hand; litterīs, by letter. “By doing” is the ablative of the gerund: ambulandō, by walking. A person who does it takes ā (see “by”, the doer); a person through whom it is done takes per. For “thanks to”, see due to.

Other words

  • per + acc. — through, by means of (a go-between, a channel)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.12.2: per explōrātōrēs Caesar certior factus est; Cic. Att. 4.14.1: mē per litterās fēcit certiōrem; Traupman 344

    Chiefly of the person who carries a thing out or brings word, and of channels such as per litterās.

Examples

  • Actiō māluimus iter facere pedibus quī incommodissimē nāvigāssēmus

    from Actium we preferred to travel on foot, after a most uncomfortable voyageCic. Att. 5.9.1

  • multae etiam istārum arborum meā manū sunt satae

    many of these trees were even planted by my own handCic. Sen. 59

  • hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

    the human mind is fed by learning and thinkingCic. Off. 1.105

  • Sōcratēn ferunt, cum ūsque ad vesperum contentius ambulāret quaesītumque esset ex eō quārē id faceret, respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem

    they say that Socrates, walking hard until evening and asked why he did it, answered that by walking he was buying in hunger, to enjoy his dinner moreCic. Tusc. 5.97

  • Ubi per explōrātōrēs Caesar certior factus est trēs jam partēs cōpiārum Helvētiōs id flūmen trādūxisse

    when Caesar learned through his scouts that the Helvetii had already taken three quarters of their forces across that riverCaes. BG 1.12.2

See also by, with, due to.
